metadata.name: PCI Data Security Standard
metadata.description: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) v4.0.1 provides a baseline of technical and operational requirements designed to protect payment account data. It applies to all entities that store, process, or transmit cardholder data and/or sensitive authentication data.
metadata.classification_reasoning: PCI DSS is a certification framework requiring formal validation through Self-Assessment Questionnaires (SAQ) or on-site assessments by Qualified Security Assessors (QSA), resulting in an Attestation of Compliance (AOC). Version 4.0.1 published June 2024, superseding v4.0 from March 2022.
metadata.framework_purpose: To protect cardholder data and reduce payment card fraud by providing a baseline of technical and operational security requirements across the payment card industry ecosystem.
metadata.framework_scope: All entities involved in payment card processing that store, process, or transmit cardholder data (CHD) and/or sensitive authentication data (SAD), including merchants, processors, acquirers, issuers, and service providers. Includes all system components in or connected to the cardholder data environment (CDE).
framework_objectives: Build and Maintain a Secure Network and Systems
metadata.target_audience: Merchants, Payment Processors, Service Providers, Acquirers, Issuers, QSAs, ISAs, and IT Security Teams handling payment card data
metadata.penalty_for_non_compliance: Non-compliance may result in fines from $5,000 to $100,000 per month imposed by payment brands, increased transaction fees, liability for fraud losses, and potential loss of ability to process payment cards.
metadata.adoption_approach: Define cardholder data environment (CDE) scope, conduct gap assessment against all requirements, develop remediation plan and implement controls, perform quarterly ASV scans, complete annual penetration testing, submit SAQ or ROC with AOC to acquiring bank.
